name: 2one Design System — graph ontology
description: The schema for the 2one knowledge graph. Defines the semantic node classes, the directional edge types (each with an allowed domain -> range and an unambiguous meaning), the decision-priority vocabulary, the provenance levels, and the conflict-resolution precedence ladder. build-graph.mjs validates every generated edge against this ontology; graph-decide.mjs reasons over it. Nothing here is derived — it is the authored contract.

Component.purpose: An implemented UI building block (Radix/shadcn primitive, a 2one-authored one, or a specific variant).

Pattern.purpose: A composed, reusable solution: a template, chart, a named UX pattern, or a component for an AI interface (a single AI-product state).

Rule.purpose: A first-class design/UX law: constraint, guideline, or anti-pattern.

Intent.purpose: A user goal / UX intent the system reasons from (e.g. submit a form).

Context.purpose: A situation or platform that conditions a decision (mobile, confirmation flow).

State.purpose: An interaction state a component can express (loading, error, selected).

AccessibilityRequirement.purpose: An a11y obligation a component or pattern must satisfy.

Brand.purpose: Brand identity: mission, voice, tone, personas.

Evidence.purpose: A checkable fact that supports a decision (e.g. an APCA contrast measurement).

Package.purpose: An external npm dependency a component pulls in.

Guide.purpose: An end-to-end build recipe (a guide that composes components/patterns into a whole surface).

meaning.MANDATORY: Must hold. A UI that breaks it is invalid.
meaning.PREFERRED: The default choice unless a higher rule or explicit context overrides.
meaning.RECOMMENDED: Should hold; deviation needs a reason.
meaning.ALTERNATIVE: A valid secondary option to a preferred one.
meaning.FORBIDDEN: Must never hold. A UI that does it is invalid.

meaning.explicit: Authored directly in a source rule, doc, or component metadata (graph/decisions.json, docs/*, brand.json).
meaning.derived: Parsed deterministically from repository source (component/token/template files).
meaning.inferred: Heuristically concluded; never authoritative on its own.

conflict_precedence.description: When two rules conflict, the category earlier in this ladder wins (tier 1 strongest); within a category the higher severity wins (forbidden > must > should > may > avoid). This mirrors rules/ux-rules.json precedence — the authoritative source — with AI preference appended as the weakest. An AI agent MUST resolve conflicts by this ladder, never by guessing. Accessibility is never traded away for brand or aesthetics.

derived_from.meaning: source token takes its value from target ramp step.

depends_on.meaning: source component imports target npm package.

has_contrast.meaning: source token participates in target contrast fact.

embodies.meaning: source (voice) is expressed by target rule.

applies_when.meaning: source rule/decision is active only in target context.

overrides.meaning: source rule takes precedence over target rule.

conflicts_with.meaning: source rule can conflict with target rule (resolve by tier).

realized_by.meaning: the target pattern/component is the preferred realisation of the source intent.

appropriate_for.meaning: source is a valid choice for target intent/context.

inappropriate_for.meaning: source must NOT be used for target intent/context.

preferred_for.meaning: source is the PREFERRED choice for target intent (over alternatives).

preferred_over.meaning: source is preferred over target for the same job.

alternative_to.meaning: source is a valid secondary option to target.

forbidden_with.meaning: source must never be composed with target.

requires.meaning: source must satisfy target a11y requirement (or include target component).

supports_state.meaning: source component can express target interaction state.

preferred_composition.meaning: source pattern's preferred make-up includes target.

demonstrates.meaning: source template is a worked example of target pattern/rule.

specializes.meaning: source is a more specific variant of target.
